assessments.reasoning: The manual’s Identifier equality algorithm compares the initial characters directly and then compares the strings after underscore removal and ASCII lowercasing. The adjoining prose confirms the ASCII-only case-insensitive comparison of the remaining letters.

challenge.method: Checked first-character case changes separately from underscore insertion and ASCII case changes after the first character, tracing each through the published algorithm.
challenge.results: For valid inputs the algorithm equates foo_bar and fOoBar, while FooBar fails the initial comparison with foo_bar. The algorithm specifically invokes ASCII lowercasing.

limitations: Only identifier equality of syntactically valid identifiers is asserted. Accepted characters, lexical adjacency and non-ASCII text handling have distinct claims.
